title: Circular timelike orbit and reduced radial stability

items.title: Lyapunov stability of Schwarzschild circular orbits in the fixed-angular-momentum radial system
items.statement:
Adopt the Schwarzschild vacuum exterior model with $m_*>0$, $s=2G_Nm_*/c^2>0$ and $f(r)=1-s/r$, together with its ideal-free-fall rule that a massive test body follows a future timelike geodesic. For a fixed angular-momentum magnitude $\ell>0$, set

$$W_\ell(r)=f(r)\left(c^2+\frac{\ell^2}{r^2}\right),\qquad r>s.$$

The equatorial reduced radial system is

$$\dot r=w,\qquad \dot w=-\frac12 W_\ell'(r),$$

where dot denotes proper-time derivative and $\ell$ is held fixed. For every circular timelike radius $r_c>3s/2$, the corresponding equilibrium is

$$z_c=(r_c,0),\qquad \ell^2=\frac{c^2s r_c^2}{2r_c-3s}.$$

Then this equilibrium is Lyapunov stable in the Euclidean phase space $(r,w)$ when $r_c>3s$, and is not Lyapunov stable when $3s/2<r_c\le3s$. At $r_c=3s$ the equilibrium is a stationary inflection of $W_\ell$, not a strict extremum, and is still not Lyapunov stable. These are conclusions about the reduced radial system at fixed $\ell$ only.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, author-hosted Chapter 1 HTML of the complete lecture notes, §§1.2.5 and 1.3.1–1.3.5 (printed pp. 24–46)
Sean Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, complete lecture notes, §7, pp. 172–179

items.physical_scope: Conditional conclusion of the adopted Schwarzschild vacuum and free-fall model for the one-dimensional timelike radial subsystem at fixed angular momentum. Lyapunov stability is only for the reduced state (r, dr/dτ); it is not stability of the full spacetime orbit, against angular-momentum perturbations, or against radiation reaction, self-force, finite-size effects, or observations.

items.title: Null scattering, the critical impact parameter, and capture in the Schwarzschild exterior model
items.statement:
Adopt the Schwarzschild exterior vacuum model with $s>0$ and the ideal-light rule that rays are future null geodesics. For an equatorial incoming ray with constants $E>0$, $L\ge0$, impact parameter $b=L/E$, and

$$H(r)=\frac{1-s/r}{r^2},\qquad b_{\rm c}=\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}s,\qquad r_{\rm ph}=\frac32s,$$

the radial first integral is $\dot r^2=E^2[1-b^2H(r)]$ as in [[lem-rpm-schwarzschild-null-geodesic-reduction]], where dot denotes affine-parameter derivative. Then:

1. If $b>b_{\rm c}$, there is a unique outer turning point $r_*(b)>r_{\rm ph}$, which is reached in finite affine parameter; the ray from infinity turns and returns to infinity. Its total azimuthal advance is

   $$\Delta\varphi=2\int_{r_*}^{\infty}\frac{b\,dr}{r^2\sqrt{1-b^2H(r)}}.$$

   This integral converges at both endpoints.
2. If $b=b_{\rm c}$, the incoming branch from infinity approaches $r_{\rm ph}$ only as affine parameter tends to $+\infty$; its azimuthal advance diverges logarithmically.
3. If $0\le b<b_{\rm c}$, the inward branch has no exterior turning point and reaches the boundary $r=s$ of the Schwarzschild exterior in finite affine parameter. Only if the ray is continued in the specified Kruskal model, once it lies in the region $U\ge0$, does the causal escape result imply that it cannot return to the right exterior.

These are geodesic-model deductions. The impact threshold is not by itself an observable shadow radius.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, author-hosted Chapter 1 HTML of the complete lecture notes, §§1.2.5 and 1.3.1–1.3.5 (printed pp. 24–46)
Sean Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, complete lecture notes, §7, pp. 176–179

items.physical_scope: Conditional geodesic predictions for ideal rays in the adopted Schwarzschild exterior model. Capture beyond r=s is asserted only conditionally in the named Kruskal extension. The statement excludes finite wavelength, wave optics, source/apparatus modelling, plasma, rotation, self-gravity, and empirical shadow or lensing claims.

items.title: Static-clock redshift, proper acceleration, and a controlled weak-field expansion in Schwarzschild
items.statement:
Let $s=2G_Nm_*/c^2>0$, $f(r)=1-s/r$, and let $r_E,r_R>s$ be the emitter and receiver radii of static observers in the adopted Schwarzschild exterior model. With $n=f^{-1/2}\partial_0$ the unit static congruence and $U=cn$ the corresponding four-velocity, the ideal-clock and geometric-optics predictions are

$$\frac{\Delta\tau_R}{\Delta\tau_E}=\frac{\omega_E}{\omega_R}=\sqrt{\frac{f(r_R)}{f(r_E)}},\qquad \frac{\omega_R}{\omega_E}=\sqrt{\frac{f(r_E)}{f(r_R)}}.$$

The proper four-acceleration magnitude required to remain static at radius $r>s$ is

$$a(r)=\sqrt{g(\nabla_UU,\nabla_UU)}=\frac{c^2s}{2r^2\sqrt{f(r)}}=\frac{G_Nm_*}{r^2\sqrt{1-s/r}}.$$

For any $0\le\rho<1$ and radii satisfying $0<s/r_E,s/r_R\le\rho$, define $x_i=s/r_i$ and write $\log:=L$ for the natural integral logarithm of [[def-integral-logarithm]]. The exact logarithmic ratio has the uniform expansion

$$\log\frac{\omega_R}{\omega_E}=\frac{s}{2}\left(\frac1{r_R}-\frac1{r_E}\right)+R,\qquad |R|\le\frac{x_E^2+x_R^2}{4(1-\rho)}.$$

These are conditional deductions of the idealized model; no measured redshift or acceleration is asserted.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, author-hosted Chapter 1 HTML of the complete lecture notes, §§1.2.5 and 1.3.1–1.3.5 (printed pp. 24–46)
Sean Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, complete lecture notes, §7, pp. 180–181

items.physical_scope: Conditional model prediction for ideal static clocks, observer energy/frequency ratios in geometric optics, and the proper acceleration required to remain static in the Schwarzschild exterior. The weak-field statement is a uniform mathematical remainder bound. No clock, spectral, acceleration, or gravitational-field measurement is asserted.

title: Circular timelike orbit and reduced radial stability — Examples

items.title: Fixed-angular-momentum stability at 2s, 3s and 4s
items.statement:
Use $s>0$ and the reduced potential $W_\ell(r)=(1-s/r)(c^2+\ell^2/r^2)$ of [[pthm-rpm-schwarzschild-circular-stability]]. At a circular orbit, $\ell^2=c^2sr_0^2/(2r_0-3s)$.

1. **Stable radial equilibrium at $r_0=4s$.** The circular value is $\ell^2=16c^2s^2/5$, and

   $$W_\ell''(4s)=\frac{2c^2s(4s-3s)}{(4s)^3(8s-3s)}=\frac{c^2}{160s^2}>0.$$

   The fixed-$\ell$ radial equilibrium is Lyapunov stable.
2. **Unstable radial equilibrium at $r_0=2s$.** Here $\ell^2=4c^2s^2$ and

   $$W_\ell''(2s)=\frac{2c^2s(2s-3s)}{(2s)^3(4s-3s)}=-\frac{c^2}{4s^2}<0.$$

   The fixed-$\ell$ equilibrium is unstable.
3. **Degenerate endpoint at $r_0=3s$.** Here $\ell^2=3c^2s^2$ and $W_\ell'(r)=c^2s(r-3s)^2/r^4$. It has a stationary inflection rather than a strict extremum, and the radial equilibrium is not Lyapunov stable by the one-sided perturbation argument in the theorem.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, author-hosted Chapter 1 HTML of the complete lecture notes, §§1.2.5 and 1.3.1–1.3.5 (printed pp. 24–46)
Sean Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, complete lecture notes, §7, pp. 174–177

items.physical_scope: Worked parameter values for the conditional Schwarzschild fixed-angular-momentum radial model; not full orbital stability or an observation.

items.title: An exact turning ray and the critical Schwarzschild impact parameter
items.statement:
Let $s>0$. The critical impact parameter is $b_c=3\sqrt3s/2$. Choose $b=2\sqrt2s>b_c$. The radial factor is $1-b^2(1-s/r)/r^2$.

1. At $r=2s$, this factor is $1-(8s^2)(1/2)/(4s^2)=0$. Because $2s>3s/2$ and $H(r)=(1-s/r)/r^2$ is strictly decreasing for $r>3s/2$, $r_*=2s$ is the unique outer turning point. The ideal incoming ray turns there and returns outward.
2. At the critical value, direct factorization gives

   $$1-b_c^2H(r)=\frac{(2r-3s)^2(r+3s)}{4r^3}.$$

   Thus the critical inward ray from infinity approaches $r=3s/2$ asymptotically, and the azimuthal integral diverges logarithmically; it does not complete a finite number of windings before reaching the circular orbit in affine parameter.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, author-hosted Chapter 1 HTML of the complete lecture notes, §§1.2.5 and 1.3.1–1.3.5 (printed pp. 24–46)

items.title: Static Schwarzschild clocks at 2s and 4s, and the near-horizon acceleration limit
items.statement:
Let $s>0$ and compare static emitter and receiver radii $r_E=2s$, $r_R=4s$ over the same Schwarzschild exterior model. Here $f(2s)=1/2$ and $f(4s)=3/4$.

1. The exact model ratios are

   $$\frac{\omega_R}{\omega_E}=\sqrt{\frac{f(2s)}{f(4s)}}=\sqrt{\frac23},\qquad \frac{\Delta\tau_R}{\Delta\tau_E}=\sqrt{\frac{f(4s)}{f(2s)}}=\sqrt{\frac32}.$$

   The static proper acceleration at $2s$ is $a(2s)=c^2/(4\sqrt2s)$.
2. Write $r=s(1+\epsilon)$ for $\epsilon>0$. The exact static proper acceleration is

   $$a(r)=\frac{c^2}{2s\sqrt\epsilon(1+\epsilon)^{3/2}},$$

   which tends to $+\infty$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$. In contrast, the curvature scalar has limit $K\to12/s^4$ by [[lem-gr-schwarzschild-curvature-and-kretschmann-scalar]], and the advanced extension chart is smooth through $r=s$ by [[lem-gr-schwarzschild-extension-chart]]. The acceleration divergence is therefore a property of maintaining a static worldline near the boundary, not evidence of a curvature blow-up there.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, author-hosted Chapter 1 HTML of the complete lecture notes, §§1.2.5 and 1.3.1–1.3.5 (printed pp. 24–46)
Sean Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, complete lecture notes, §7, pp. 180–181

items.physical_scope: Worked model calculation for ideal static observers and an ideal light ray. The near-horizon acceleration is a model requirement for static motion, not an observation; curvature and extension statements are geometric properties of the specified Schwarzschild model.

items.title: Formal nonrelativistic limit of the repulsive Coulomb scattering angle
items.statement:
Fix $m,\kappa,K,b>0$ and let $c\to\infty$ with $W_c=mc^2+K$ and $J_c=b\sqrt{A_c}$, where $A_c=(W_c^2-m^2c^4)/c^2$. For sufficiently large $c$, $J_c>\kappa/c$ because $J_c^2-\kappa^2/c^2\to2mKb^2>0$.

1. The relativistic scattering angle tends to the nonrelativistic repulsive Coulomb angle:

   $$\theta_c\longrightarrow2\arctan\left(\frac{\kappa}{2Kb}\right).$$

   This agrees with [[thm-cm-coulomb-scattering]] at kinetic energy $K$ and impact parameter $b$.
2. The limit compares ideal mathematical model formulas while holding the indicated parameters fixed; it supplies no experimental evidence for either model.

items.physical_scope: Formal c-to-infinity limit of exact model formulas at fixed rest mass, Coulomb coupling, Newtonian kinetic energy, and impact parameter. It is not a measured comparison or empirical validation.
